findings.element: Section 1 — the toggle on the date row when the no-limit admin flag is off
findings.finding: The date row toggle renders at full strength — pixel-identical to the two live toggles directly above and below it — but its click handler returns early and does nothing, with no feedback of any kind.
findings.user_impact: Users trying to widen the search to invoices of any age click a toggle that appears fully functional, get zero response, and click again — the exact dead-click pattern KF-4 identifies as the product densest friction, made worse because the plan-gated master switch in the same overlay does dim itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the date toggle the same visibly non-interactive treatment already used for the plan-gated master switch, and keep the lock glyph plus the existing hint as the explanation.

evidence.action: Opened the overlay, turned the rule on with the admin flag left off, then clicked the date row toggle three times and read back its class and computed style.
evidence.observed: Class stayed toggle on across all three clicks, the row label stayed unchanged, no message appeared, and computed opacity was 1 — identical to the working Customer and invoice-number toggles; the only differences are cursor:not-allowed and a small grey lock glyph.

findings.element: Overlay chrome — Escape key, header close and footer Cancel
findings.finding: All three exits silently discard every unsaved edit in the rule builder with no confirmation and no undo.
findings.user_impact: A user who has spent minutes assembling a multi-row rule loses all of it to a single stray Escape — the reflex for dismissing a dropdown — and has to rebuild the whole configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: When the working copy differs from the saved rule, intercept Escape, close and Cancel with a Discard your changes? confirmation, and let Escape only dismiss that confirmation.

evidence.action: Turned the rule on, clicked Add condition twice, changed Days either side to 45, then dispatched a single Escape keypress and reopened the overlay.
evidence.observed: The overlay closed immediately, no confirmation was shown, and reopening restored the saved state — the three condition rows and the 45-day window were gone.

findings.element: Master switch reference card vs the initial contents of sections 1 and 2 after the switch is turned on
findings.finding: The off-state card states Nothing is pre-filled, but turning the switch on delivers a fully populated rule — all three scope rows on and a condition row already set to Invoice note is equal to Memo on statement — and Save is immediately enabled.
findings.user_impact: A user who trusts that sentence assumes an empty canvas and saves what looks like a starting point, silently committing a statement-memo condition they never chose that is far narrower than the default matcher they meant to replace, so payments that used to match stop matching.
findings.suggested_fix: Either start section 2 with no condition rows and correct the sentence to describe only that the saved rule is untouched until Save, or keep the pre-fill and relabel it explicitly as a starting template the user must review.

evidence.action: Loaded the prototype in Chrome, read the off-state reference card, clicked the master switch on, and inspected sections 1-3 and the Save button.
evidence.observed: Card reads Nothing is pre-filled; after the click all three scope rows are on with a 90-day window, section 2 already contains one condition row, and Save is enabled with the message Applies to Stripe — mzkt.by only.

findings.element: Overlay footer and the GSP Payment application status chip, while Apply payments to invoices is off
findings.finding: With the prerequisite off, the rule still saves and every confirmation signal reports success — Save enabled, footer says it applies to this integration, and the GSP row then shows a green Custom rule chip — even though the rule can never run, and the overlay offers no control to turn the prerequisite on.
findings.user_impact: The user finishes the task, receives three separate confirmations that the rule is live, and walks away while no payment is ever matched — and to fix it they must abandon the overlay and hunt for a different toggle, because the warning banner is text only.
findings.suggested_fix: While the prerequisite is off, put the prerequisite toggle inside the overlay warning banner, replace the footer message with an inert-state warning, and mark the GSP chip as inactive rather than green.

evidence.action: With the overlay open and a rule configured, unchecked the environment Apply payments to invoices flag, then read the footer, counted actionable controls in the warning banner, and clicked Save.
evidence.observed: Save was enabled, the footer read Applies to Stripe — mzkt.by only., the warning banner contained 0 buttons or links, Save closed the overlay successfully, and the GSP row then rendered Payment application Custom rule.

findings.element: Section 1 — Days either side number input
findings.finding: An out-of-range value is silently rewritten to the maximum on commit, with no message and no statement of the limit anywhere in the product UI.
findings.user_impact: A user who deliberately enters a wide window sees the number quietly become a different one, cannot tell whether the field is broken or capped, and may not notice at all.
findings.suggested_fix: State the accepted range in the field label or helper text and, when a value is clamped, show an inline note naming the limit that was applied.

evidence.action: Typed 999 into Days either side and dispatched the change event, then read the field value, any rendered error text and the footer message.
evidence.observed: The field showed 365, no error or hint about the cap was rendered, and the maximum of 365 is written down only inside the purple assumption annotation, which is not product UI.

gaps: Error findability was not verifiable: the map never records whether the inline error is in view when Save is disabled, and no short-viewport pass was run.
The Generic customer state was never exercised in the state map; whether it should also affect the scope validity guard (FDD Q4 open) is unverified.
Applies to this integration only could not be tested: the prototype exposes a single integration, so whether the shared cancel-sync value is also shared across other integrations is unknown.
Condition rows with the same source and target were never exercised, so it is unknown whether the builder warns about a condition that can never be satisfied or one that duplicates a scope row.
